title: When a held-out check freezes: on its own failure seen, or with the cut's checks
situation: The freeze concept freezes an example only once its check has been seen to fail. In the meaning-roles fix round the lead realized held-out checks as frozen together with the cut's checks: the judgment folder is frozen from the first time any of the cut's checks is frozen. The frozen visible checks of workflow/31 to 36 require this: they freeze the visible checks only, then expect a file in the judgment folder refused. In judgment, one assayer (Anthropic family) rejected it: a held-out check written after the first freeze (a check-writer still at work, or a burned case's cold replacement under 0103) is frozen before it has been seen to fail, and only the architect can then write it. The other assayer (Google family) accepted it as keeping to the concept. The assayers disagree, and the fix needs a frozen check changed, which is the architect's alone.
decision: Recommended: a held-out check freezes like a visible one, by the freeze act that names it once it has been seen to fail. The judgment folder is never frozen by implication. The architect rules on the visible freeze checks, which then name their held-out check in the freeze instead of expecting it frozen by implication. The held-out example text stays frozen from the cut's opening.
consequences: Accepted, the freeze-record work lists only the held-out checks the freeze act names. The architect applies the ruling to the frozen visible freeze checks, and the cut's next round rebuilds against them. Until then the realization in the branch stands: held-out checks freeze with the cut's first freeze.
